findings.title: Queue pool is shared across assignments and is shut down when any strategy closes, so a rebalance drops results
findings.body: `create_with_partitions` builds a new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` around the same `self.queue_pool` every time Arroyo assigns partitions. Arroyo closes the previous strategy on revoke, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` / `terminate()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()` (queue_consumer.py lines 335-342). That shuts down the shared queues and worker threads for the new strategy too. Later `submit()` calls hit `queue.ShutDown` on `put`, which the `except` in `submit` swallows after marking the offset complete. The offset is then committed without the result ever being processed, so results are silently lost after any rebalance. The pool should be created per strategy, or shutdown should only happen at factory shutdown.

findings.title: A missing offset in the sequence blocks commits permanently
findings.body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks as soon as `offset not in all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous (transaction/control markers, compaction, seeks). Any gap that is never submitted means `highest_committable` never advances past it, so the partition's committed offset stops moving for the life of the process and lag grows without bound. On restart, everything after the gap is reprocessed. The gap should be treated as complete, or the scan should be bounded to offsets actually seen (for example, iterate over the sorted `all_offsets` set instead of every integer in the range).

findings.title: Docstring claims backpressure, but the queues are unbounded
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` documents 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but `FixedQueuePool` creates `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, so `put` never blocks. If workers fall behind, the in-memory backlog grows without limit, and the Kafka consumer keeps polling and buffering messages. Either bound the queues (blocking submit) or fix the docstring and add a memory safeguard.

findings.title: Arroyo commit callback is invoked from a background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own daemon thread and calls `commit_function`, which forwards to the Arroyo `commit` callback that the StreamProcessor provides. That callback was built for the processor thread. Calling it concurrently with the main poll/processing loop can race on consumer state, and the callback can run after the processor has begun shutting down. Commits should be marshalled back to the processor thread (for example in `poll()`), or the thread-safety of the callback should be confirmed and documented.

findings.title: Flaky assertion: total_items > 0 right after submit
findings.body: `test_stats_reporting` submits 10 items with a 4-group key, then immediately asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. The worker threads start consuming as soon as items are put, so they can drain all items before `get_stats()` runs, making this assertion fail intermittently. The test should not depend on timing for this check.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the behavior it describes
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is documented as 'errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages', and the mock makes the first call raise. The worker's `finally` marks offset 100 complete, so offset 101 is committable and the commit thread should commit it. The final assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` requires that no commit happened, which contradicts the test's own intent. It will fail when commits happen, and when they don't it passes for the wrong reason. The assertion should expect commit 102 (next offset after 101) for the partition.

findings.title: Transaction name uses the 'monitors.' prefix copied from another consumer
findings.body: The worker starts transactions named `monitors.{identifier}.worker_{id}`, and `ResultProcessor` uses the same `monitors.` prefix. This is an uptime/remote-subscriptions consumer, so these traces will be grouped under the monitors namespace and be hard to find or filter. The name should use a remote-subscriptions or uptime prefix.
